title: Contract obligation workbench

stages.name: parseObligations
stages.algorithm: Extract atomic obligations with actor, beneficiary, trigger, deadline, and exceptions. Separate descriptions and aspirations from operative provisions, retain cross-references, and preserve unknown roles rather than assigning responsibility from nearby names.
stages.gate: Each obligation retains all material conditions and supporting clause spans.

stages.name: resolveInteractions
stages.algorithm: Interpret cross-references and interactions among provisions under the supplied authority hierarchy. Distinguish a narrow exception from replacement of an entire obligation and preserve unresolved conflicts for qualified review instead of guessing a priority rule.
stages.gate: Every relation has scope and source support; conflict is not silently converted into supersession.

stages.name: assessEvents
stages.algorithm: Compare incoming operational events with contractual triggers and conditions. Distinguish an allegation that a trigger occurred from established evidence, and request the smallest missing fact when activation would materially change a duty or deadline.
stages.gate: Trigger activation requires evidence under the selected interpretation version.

stages.name: planPerformance
stages.algorithm: Turn active obligations into bounded tasks with ownership, dependencies, and exact computed dates. Preserve legal interpretation separately from operational scheduling and identify impossible or conflicting task requirements before issuing commitments.
stages.gate: No unowned active obligation; dates use the configured calendar and explicit deadline rule.

stages.name: verifyDischarge
stages.algorithm: Compare completed actions with the actual duty and any acceptance condition. Distinguish performance from waiver or settlement, record reviewer-approved interpretations, and keep disputed discharge visible rather than closing on an internal completion flag.
stages.gate: Satisfaction is supported; waivers require their own scoped authority evidence.

operational_details: A deadline uses business days: store the agreed calendar rather than assuming local weekends.
A party changes its legal name: preserve identity and do not treat it as a new counterparty automatically.
A notice is sent to the wrong address: separate dispatch from contractually effective notice.
A clause is disputed: display alternative operational consequences pending review.
A confidential clause supports a shared task: expose only the minimum necessary instruction.
representative_episode: An agreement requires notice after a verified outage, with a narrow emergency exception that changes timing but not the notice obligation.
independent_truth_basis: Generated contracts with explicit trigger truth, exception scope, event histories, and exact expected obligation states.
